summary: Full-extraction pass over 16 UK documents (CMA, FCA/PRA, Fisher review, HMRC Strengthened Reward Scheme, Treasury budgets and speeches, Anti-Corruption Strategy, written question, SFO). Most are policy texts whose rules and events were already recorded; the Fisher review and SFO speeches add relayed figures on US and Canadian programmes and on UK nationals tipping US programmes.

observations.quote: with 774 UK nationals giving tips to the four different US programmes between 2012 and 2023
observations.notes: Relayed by the UK Fisher review (official Home Office publication) from another source, hence 'reported'. The figure is an estimate by Spotlight on Corruption (footnote 376, blog of 12 Mar 2023). UK nationals who gave tips to the four US programmes (not named; presumably SEC, CFTC, IRS, FinCEN or DOJ), counted as persons. No single program_id because it covers several programmes.

observations.quote: I think 86% of the $2.2 billion in civil settlements and judgments recovered by the US Department of Justice were based on whistleblower information.
observations.notes: Period not stated in the speech (dataset convention: period_basis 'unspecified', period filed as up to the speech date); not inferred. program_rules.notes: An initial no-names contact is possible, but the CMA needs the informant's identity before going further, so a reward cannot be earned anonymously. valid_from left empty: the page was first published 31 Mar 2014 and later updated; the version read is the current one.

program_rules.quote: Under section 26, HMRC makes discretionary payments to individuals who report suspected tax fraud. Unlike some international models, the size of the reward is not linked to the amount of tax recovered.
program_rules.notes: Relayed by the Fisher review (secondary description, not the law itself); valid_from left empty because the review does not date the rule. Agrees with the rows from the HMRC annual reports.

cases.summary: Former UBS wealth manager awarded US$104 million under the IRS programme for reporting a tax evasion scheme at UBS; he was also convicted for his part and served a 40-month sentence. The review says the case was followed by more self-reports and participation in the programme, which led to over US$11 billion collected in back taxes and the prosecution of several banks.
cases.location: PDF p. 135 (printed p. 129), case study box after para 536
cases.quote: It was under the IRS programme that Bradley Birkenfeld was awarded US $104 million for blowing the whistle on a tax evasion scheme at the Swiss bank UBS.
cases.notes: Relayed (footnote 395 cites a Kohn, Kohn & Colapinto law-firm page). Date not given in the review. Birkenfeld went public himself (already named in c-365aae9cfc). The 'over US $11 billion' in back taxes is not attributed to whistleblower information alone (self-reports), so it is kept here rather than as an observation.

gaps: Korea National Tax Service informant rewards (5-20%) and foreign financial account reporting rewards (5-15%) are described in the Fisher review (para 547) but the dataset has no programme for them.

FCA whistleblowing case volumes (FCA/PRA 2014 note) and SFO whistleblowing disclosures (Fisher review, Anti-Corruption Strategy) are not recorded: no programme exists for those protection-only channels.
leads: Proposed rule 'tax_withheld_pct' (gbr-hmrc-srs, 45%) needs a decision; enters into force only on Royal Assent to Finance Bill 2026-27.

ledger.contains: CMA press release (6 Jun 2023): cartel informant reward cap raised from £100,000 to £250,000; rewards discretionary, paid if information is significant and leads to enforcement; reward separate from leniency, normally not for leniency applicants unless their role was peripheral. Also general cartel sanctions (fines up to 10% of turnover, up to 5 years' prison, up to 15 years' director disqualification), which are not about the reward programme. The two cap rules and the rule-change event were already recorded; no statistics on rewards paid.

CMA guidance 'Rewards for information about cartels' (first published 31 Mar 2014, current version states the £250,000 cap): why rewards are offered, what a cartel is, hotline, confidentiality, process (no-names first contact, identity then required), discretionary rewards set by value of information, harm stopped, effort and risk; paid only at the end of an investigation, expenses reimbursed; leniency applicants normally not rewarded; complainant businesses unlikely to get rewards. Cartel sanctions (10% of turnover, 5 years' prison, 15 years' disqualification) are not about the programme. No statistics. The £250,000 cap is already recorded from the 2023 news release (not duplicated); the discretionary rule was already recorded; this pass adds the anonymous-filing rule.

FCA/PRA note to the Treasury Select Committee (Jul 2014) rejecting financial incentives for whistleblowers: US research findings, moral hazards, comparison with CMA/HMRC informant (CHIS) payments, planned annual whistleblowing reports. Numbers present are about FCA whistleblowing case volumes, not a reward programme (cases up 55% 2011-2012 and 42% 2012-2013; expected to rise about 30% in 2014 to around 1,200; under 1% of cases lead to financial penalties) and are out of scope because the dataset has no FCA programme. Its two events (BIS response 25 Jun 2014; FCA/PRA decision) were already recorded.

Independent Review of Disclosure and Fraud Offences, second report (280 pp.). Only chapter 11 'Whistleblower Incentivisation' (PDF pp. 131-148) and the recommendation lists (pp. 15, 263) concern reward programmes; the rest covers fraud trends, platforms, data-sharing, investigation, powers, penalties, DPAs and is out of scope. Chapter 11 contents: US, Canadian and Korean programmes described (rules and relayed figures), UK HMRC and CMA schemes, Ipsos poll (70% support rewards; 28/42/19/5/1%, out of scope: opinion, not programme data), Metropolitan Police CHIS payments 2022/23 £1,041,442.60 (out of scope: covert sources, no programme), SFO 167 qualifying whistleblowing disclosures 2024/25, acted on 153 (out of scope: SFO has no reward programme), Recommendations 15-18 (SFO rewards, false-report and harassment offences, arbitration panel). This pass adds 11 relayed observations (UK nationals tipping US programmes; SEC FY2023/FY2024; CFTC cumulative; CRA OTIP to 2019; OSC 2016-2022), 19 relayed rules, and the Birkenfeld award as a case. HMRC 2022/23 and 2023/24 totals and Recommendation 15 event were already recorded. Not recorded: Korea NTS informant rewards (5-20%) and foreign financial account rewards (5-15%) because the dataset has no programme for them; 'fewer than 1%' of US whistleblowers rewarded (unattributed, no programme or period); DOJ pilot programme description (no numbers).

One-page draft Finance Bill clause inserting s.974A ITA 2007: HMRC must deduct income tax at the additional rate from informant rewards under the Strengthened Reward Scheme (published 26 Nov 2025) or any scheme designated by Treasury regulations. Gives no rate figure or date; the 45% withholding rule and the 13 Jul 2026 event are recorded from the companion tax information and impact note (gbr-hmrc-srs-withholding-tiin-2026). Not yet enacted.

GOV.UK guidance for the Strengthened Reward Scheme (26 Nov 2025): reward 15-30% of tax collected (excluding penalties and interest) when information leads to at least £1.5 million collected; discretionary; exclusions (civil servants, the taxpayer involved, information already known, illegal funding risk, legal duty, acting for others, second-hand from ineligible persons, anonymous reports); how to report (form character limits of 1,200 and 500 are not programme data); no feedback; years may pass before payment. All five rules and the launch event were already recorded; nothing further in scope.

HMRC tax information and impact note (13 Jul 2026) on withholding income tax at the 45% additional rate from Strengthened Reward Scheme rewards (new s.974A ITA 2007), effective from Royal Assent to Finance Bill 2026-27; restates scheme rules (over £1.5 million recovered, up to 30%, excluding penalties and interest; already recorded); current law (s.26 CRCA 2005, rewards taxable as trading or miscellaneous income). Exchequer impact table prints 'Nil' for 2025-26 to 2030-31 for the withholding mechanism (a word, not recorded as 0; the scheme's own costing is in the policy costings document); no operational cost. The event was already recorded; this pass adds the 45% withholding as a proposed rule (tax_withheld_pct).

Autumn Budget 2024 (HTML, whole document searched): the only passage on the programme is the one-line commitment to strengthen HMRC's informant reward scheme (Chapter 5, 'Closing the tax gap'), already recorded as an event. No programme figures; the rest of the Budget is out of scope.

Budget 2025 (HTML, whole document searched): para 3.3 mentions launching a strengthened informant reward scheme modelled on the US; section 5.9 'Rewards for informants of high-value tax fraud' says rewards up to 30% where over £1.5 million is recovered, with immediate effect (26 Nov 2025). These rules and the launch are already recorded from HMRC's guidance. Table 4.1 prints only the aggregate line 'HMRC: Further measures to close the tax gap' (+75m to +2,590m, 2025-26 to 2030-31), which covers many measures and is out of scope; the informant measure's own costing is in the policy costings document. Nothing new added.

Budget 2025 policy costings (128 pp.); only p. 104 'Rewards for informants of high value tax fraud' concerns the programme: measure description (over £1.5 million, up to 30%, effective 26 Nov 2025), tax base, behavioural-response costing, Exchequer impact 2025-26 to 2030-31 (+0, +0, +10, +55, +95, +65 £m; all six already recorded as exchequer_yield_forecast). The rest of the document costs other measures and is out of scope. Nothing new added.

Exchequer Secretary's speech on 20 years of HMRC (11 Mar 2025): announces a new HMRC informant reward scheme later in 2025, inspired by US and Canadian models, paying a percentage of tax collected and complementing the existing scheme (already recorded as an event). Other figures (tax gap £6.5bn a year by 2029/30, director disqualifications, 35 million taxpayers) are not about the programme.

UK Anti-Corruption Strategy 2025 (121 pp., whole text searched). On rewards: commitment 1.1.3 (para 39.III, due 2026) to consider the Fisher review and assess financial incentive schemes for reporting economic crime (already recorded as an event); 1.1.4 (due 2027) reform whistleblowing in employment. Figures present but out of scope: SFO Intelligence Division about 1,450 referrals and 167 whistleblowing disclosures in 2024-25 (footnote 41; SFO has no reward programme), IACCC requests and assets, a Cardiff Council whistleblower-initiated bribery case (no reward). Nothing new added.

Written question UIN 93208 (tabled 20 Nov 2025, answered 27 Nov 2025): the scheme launched 26 Nov 2025; reward 15-30% when information leads to more than £1.5M tax collected (rules already recorded from HMRC guidance); HMRC will keep publishing annual totals but not the number or size of rewards (already recorded as an event). Nothing new added.

SFO news story on its 2025-26 Business Plan (3 Apr 2025): the plan includes advancing a whistleblower incentivisation scheme (already recorded as an event). Other figures (eight new investigations, charge within 15 months, document review up to 40% faster) are not about a reward programme.

SFO Interim Director's speech in New York (3 Jun 2026): SFO priorities; support for an SFO whistleblower incentivisation scheme (already recorded as an event); over 700 UK nationals gave intelligence to four US programmes 2012-2023 (added). Other figures are about SFO casework, not a reward programme (Ultra Electronics DPA £10 million penalty and £4.8 million costs, self-report service times, 5 million documents per case, AOG Technics 60,000 parts, £70 million investment fraud).

SFO Director Ephgrave's first speech (RUSI, 13 Feb 2024): 'we should pay whistleblowers' (already recorded as an event); US DOJ figure ($2.2 billion civil settlements and judgments, 86% based on whistleblower information; added, with the 86% in notes); over 700 UK whistleblowers engaged US law enforcement since 2012 (added). Other figures are SFO casework, not a reward programme (40,000 victims, Buy2Let £88m, Airbus €1bn DPA, Glencore £280m, £1.1bn to the Treasury in five years, 317% return, 48m documents, 25% of budget on disclosure).
